content.title: About
content.content: Salami is a smoked‑cured sausage made from any type of meat (pork, beef, poultry, etc.) with reduced fat content. During production part of the fat is removed, and the lean meat blend is seasoned with spices, salt and sometimes wine. The result is an aromatic, mildly spicy product with the characteristic smoky flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Salami originates from Italy, especially the regions of Emilia‑Romagna and Tuscany.
Traditionally it is aged from several weeks to several months, allowing deep flavor development.
Reduced‑fat versions are lower in calories while retaining most of the protein.
Salami is commonly used on pizza, in pasta dishes, sandwiches, and as a wine snack.
Different meat bases give distinct tastes: beef makes it richer, poultry makes it lighter.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Salami provides high‑quality animal protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Reduced fat
items.content: Lower fat content helps keep the calorie count down, useful for weight management.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: The meat supplies heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant iron.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Salami contains vitamin B12, niacin and riboflavin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Zinc content
items.content: Zinc from the meat supports immune function and wound healing.

items.title: Sodium level
items.content: Salami is typically high in salt; people with hypertension should limit intake.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Some varieties contain nitrites, which in large amounts are considered undesirable.

items.title: Meat allergy
items.content: Rare individuals allergic to certain meats may experience reactions.

items.title: Heat treatment
items.content: Over‑heating salami can produce acrylamide, a potential carcinogen.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Salami can be enjoyed as a snack, sliced thin for sandwiches, added to salads, pasta, pizza, or quickly warmed in a pan for hot dishes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store salami in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C in its original packaging or an airtight container. For longer storage (over 2‑3 weeks) freeze it. Discard any product with off‑odors or discoloration.
